get.summary: Whether the instance is answering, and which build it is.
The licence and notice of every third-party package this instance includes, generated and gated by `check:notices`.

Rooms, riders, tick lateness and refusals in the Prometheus text format — only when the operator turned it on (OYL_INSTANCE_METRICS), and only for a request carrying the operator’s token as `Authorization: Bearer`; `not_found` otherwise. No label is an athlete, a name, a room or a coordinate.
This specification.
Whether riders may be sent here yet: the database answers, its migrations are at head, and every room worker is alive (#791). 503 with the same body when not.
Where the exact source of the running build is — the offer AGPL-3.0 §13 requires (ADR 0036 D-6).

delete.summary: Remove your account from THIS instance: every row, and every original file no other rider also sent. It cannot reach a copy anyone already downloaded, or another instance. Safe to repeat after a failure.

get.summary: Everything this instance holds about you, machine-readable: every activity’s signed record and the address of its original file — your own true track, unobfuscated — every item as you sent it, your public keys, your names, your results, your blocks, the reports you made and the recovery addresses you gave. Says what it leaves out, and why.

schema.description: `onyourleft.instance-account` version 1: `athlete`, `displayNameChanges`, `deviceKeys` (public only), `recoveryEmail`, `activities` (each with its `record` and its `file` address), `items`, `results`, `blocks`, `reports`, `recoveryEmailConfirmations` and `notIncluded`.

get.summary: Your activities, newest first: `?limit=` (1–200, default 50) and `?cursor=` from the page before. One query a page, and stable while activities are added.
One of your activities, by the SHA-256 of its file: what its record claims, and the signed record itself.

record.description: A signed activity record, ADR 0014’s format: seven members, the signature over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the other six.

get.summary: One of your activities’ samples — power, heart rate, cadence, speed, altitude and distance, never a position — in full, or at `?points=` (2–10 000) for a chart: each point the mean of its share of the ride, a gap left as `null`.
What another rider may see of an athlete: the display name, and nothing else.
This athlete’s own account: whether it is approved, when they confirmed they are 18 or over, any moderator role, and whether they may join a public room — and if not, every reason why.

post.summary: Confirm that the rider is 18 or over, which public rooms require (ruling Q5). Only the confirmation and its date are kept: no date of birth is asked for or stored.
A single-use nonce, good for 60 seconds, for a device to sign with its key. Rate-limited per key and per address.

get.summary: This athlete’s device keys: when each was added and last used, and which is asking.

post.summary: Revoke one of this athlete’s device keys and its sessions. The last key needs one of the athlete’s recovery codes, which is checked and not spent.
Change the display name: 1–32 characters, no control, bidirectional or invisible character. Rate-limited, and the old name is kept for moderation.
Add this device’s key to the athlete whose other device minted the code, with a signed `oyl-link-v1` statement.

401.description: One of `wrong_purpose`, `wrong_instance`, `challenge_unknown`, `challenge_used`, `challenge_expired`, `bad_signature`, `code_unknown`, `code_used`, `code_expired`, in the one error shape.

post.summary: A single-use code, good for 5 minutes, that adds another device’s own key to this athlete.
Add this device’s key to an athlete with a recovery code, or with an emailed token where the operator enabled email recovery, and a signed `oyl-recover-v1` statement.

401.description: One of `wrong_purpose`, `wrong_instance`, `challenge_unknown`, `challenge_used`, `challenge_expired`, `bad_signature`, `code_unknown`, `code_used`, `code_expired`, in the one error shape.

post.summary: Email a single-use recovery link to an address, if an athlete registered it. The same answer either way. `not_found` where the operator has not enabled email recovery.

Give an address for email recovery: a single-use link, good for 24 hours, is mailed to it, and the address recovers nothing until that link is followed. The same answer whether or not the address is already held. `rate_limited` when this athlete has given addresses too often this hour; `internal` when the mail could not be sent, and then nothing is stored. `not_found` where the operator has not enabled email recovery.
Follow the link mailed to a recovery address, signed in as the athlete who gave it: the address is bound, replacing any earlier one. `address_in_use` when it is already another account’s.

401.description: One of `unauthenticated`, `code_unknown`, `code_used`, `code_expired`, in the one error shape.

post.summary: Sign in with a signed `oyl-auth-v1` statement. A key the instance has not seen registers a new athlete as the registration mode allows — awaiting approval by default — and only then are the recovery codes in the answer. New registrations are rate-limited per client address.

401.description: One of `wrong_purpose`, `wrong_instance`, `challenge_unknown`, `challenge_used`, `challenge_expired`, `bad_signature`, `key_revoked`, `code_unknown`, `code_used`, `code_expired`, in the one error shape.

403.description: One of `registration_closed`, `account_suspended`, `registration_refused`, in the one error shape.

get.summary: Who this session is: the athlete, as other riders see them.

delete.summary: Sign out: the session is revoked on the instance, not only forgotten by the device.

get.summary: The athletes this athlete has blocked.

post.summary: Block an athlete: neither of you sees or reaches the other, whoever blocked whom. Answers the same whether or not the athlete exists, and is kept for any well-formed id. An account may hold 1000 blocks.

delete.summary: Remove a block this athlete made. Answers the same whether or not there was one.

post.summary: Hide an athlete’s display name from other riders until they choose another. Written to the moderation log.
Suspend an account: every one of its keys is refused, its sessions end, and other riders stop seeing it. Nothing it owns is deleted. Written to the moderation log.
Lift a suspension. Written to the moderation log.
A single-use invitation, good for seven days, for an instance whose registration is invite-only. Written to the moderation log.

get.summary: Every moderator action, oldest first. Append-only.
The approval queue (#775): every athlete awaiting a moderator’s decision, oldest first, and whether each has confirmed they are 18 or over.

post.summary: Approve an account awaiting approval. Written to the moderation log.
Refuse an account awaiting approval: its every key is refused at sign-in from then on. Written to the moderation log.

get.summary: The moderators’ queue: every report not yet decided, oldest first.

post.summary: Dismiss a report, with a reason. Written to the moderation log.
Report an athlete to this instance’s moderators, with a reason. Rate-limited per reporter. Answers the same whether or not the athlete exists.
Starts a race’s countdown, for an athlete seated in it. Provisional: who may start a race is #785’s to decide.
A ticket for one room’s WebSocket hello: single use, 30 seconds. The socket never carries the session token. A public room needs an eligible account (`GET /v1/auth/account`).

get.summary: The original activity file, byte for byte, as it was sent: the rider’s own true track, unobfuscated. Only to an athlete who holds a record of it.

post.summary: Store a write-up, a side-camera report (its pose summary inside), a goal, a note or a reference document, exactly as the device sends it. The device’s copy is canonical: a later put replaces it.

get.summary: One of your items, byte for byte as it was sent.

delete.summary: Delete one of your items — or, as `activity`, a ride by its content hash, its file with it unless another rider sent the same bytes. A tombstone stays in the manifest so your other devices learn of it.

get.summary: Everything you have synced, tombstones included, in the order it arrived: `?limit=` (1–200) and `?cursor=`, a (receivedAt, id) position — so paging while other devices sync repeats nothing and skips nothing that was there.

post.summary: Send a signed activity record with its original file (base64). Checked in order — the file’s type from its bytes, that it decodes, the record’s signature and content hash, that the key is yours — and stored only if every check passes. The same file sent again answers the first record.

record.description: A signed activity record, ADR 0014’s format: seven members, the signature over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the other six.

422.description: One of `file_undecodable`, `record_malformed`, `record_unsupported`, `record_signature_mismatch`, `record_content_mismatch`, `record_not_your_key`, in the one error shape.

get.summary: One of your signed records, by the SHA-256 of its file. A device verifies it, and the file, before it writes anything.

record.description: A signed activity record, ADR 0014’s format: seven members, the signature over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the other six.

post.summary: Say whether another rider may race a ghost of one of your rides, by the SHA-256 of its file. Off unless you set it, and revocable: a ride set back to false is not served as raceable on the next read. Not part of the signed record, and never inferred from how a ride is shared.

session.description: A session token from `POST /v1/auth/session`. Never a WebSocket credential: a room takes a ticket.
